item.content:encoded:
Collapsing so as not to clutter discussion page with arguments
– hide block

Sorry, that exceeds the maximum safe load for my bellief suspenders.

Fair enough, though I will point out that this article is explicitly intended as a sequel to a previous -J crosslinked in the description. So even though this universe is silly and unrealistic, there is the implication that both these articles are taking place in the same universe. But frankly, it's a joke, so you're not actually expected to believe in it anyway. I'm a little confused as to why this is all even an issue to begin with, really.

The reason I trimmed your comment was because I agreed with the first part—
that -J articles don't exist in the general consensus universe. It's only the second part that I found debatable. I wasn't trying to intentionally misrepresent your opinion, and I apologize for doing so. I only wanted to focus on the points which I felt warranted further discussion.

It wasn't immediately clear to me that you meant it must necessarily be one case or the other, but I think I get what you're saying now. I suppose, then, this would be classified as a parody piece, but I don't think the fact that this is external to the 'canon' means it has to be considered external to the contest as well.

The only requirements (to my understanding) are a shared doomsday amongst entries—heck, ARD said they don't even have to be the same doomsday as long as they share a scenario name. If you wish to argue whether or not this constitutes an acceptable contest entry, that's probably an issue to bring up with the contest organizers via PM, rather in this discussion page.

Since our doomsday premise is intentionally silly, having a -J as an entry seemed fun and fitting. And that's really all this is about—just messing around and writing for the fun of it. Nobody's trying to pull one over on anyone here. I'm not sure what the reference to my entry is about, but at the end of the day, if you dislike one or all of our entries, I respect that. I write all this to explain where I'm coming from, but if you simply don't feel the same way about things, that's cool with me.

item.content:encoded:
Since -J articles don't exist […] as in-universe jokes

That is debatable.

It occurs to me that the way you trimmed my quote so that it utterly distorts what I meant may have been intentional. I think maybe you misunderstood me.

I am saying that -J articles are supposedly "not canon" (even in the "there is no canon" paradigm) according to the general consensus, anyway. Either they only exist out-of-universe, and there isn't a fictional writer or assumed reader, or they exist in-universe as jokes written by fictional writers for a fictional audience.

In the former case, I don't think this works as a contest entry because, as a parody of your team's entries, it is external to the contest. If it is supposed to be the latter case it requires someone familiar with both Foundation and Centre documents, who has Apollyon clearance, who is writing a joke about the recent end of the world intended for a similarly informed audience.

Who is this reader? Who is the author? Is their keyboard covered in saliva because they have fists like concrete hams?
